## SNP differences between pairs

```{r}

## This tables was obtained with the code bcftools gtcheck  -u GT,GT strain_118_variants_diploid.vcf

raw_lines <- read_lines("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sohini5981/AVT_SS/refs/heads/main/Data/strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv?token=GHSAT0AAAAAAEB5NZNICNZ5L2YG7GHWP4FI2TIXJKA")

# Keep only the actual data rows (they start with "DCv2", not "#DCv2" or "INFO")
data_lines <- raw_lines[startsWith(raw_lines, "DCv2")]
#View(data_lines)
gtcheck_data <- read_tsv(
  I(data_lines),   # I() tells read_tsv to treat this as literal text, not a filepath
  col_names = c("Tag", "Query_Sample", "Genotyped_Sample", "Discordance",
                "Avg_neg_log_P_HWE", "Sites_compared", "Matching_genotypes")
)

#View(gtcheck_data)
gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>% dplyr::select(-Tag)

### Not all of the genotypes that have been compared are paris: 

Pairs <- read_excel(here("Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx"))
View(Pairs)
Pairs <- Pairs %>% filter(!is.na(Pairs))

pairs_wide <- Pairs %>%
  select(Strain_Code, Morphology, Pairs) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Morphology, values_from = Strain_Code)
View(pairs_wide)

### I am not interested in which is teh query_sample and which one is the genotyped_sample in the strain_118_variants_pairwise_mismatches.tsv

### Sort the two strain names alphabetically first, so the same pair always produces the same key regardless of which strain in gtcheck is query or genotyped

pairs_wide <- pairs_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>% ## rowwise() always goes paired with ungroup(). rowwise() function converts a dataframe. into a special grouped form where every single row is treated as its own individual group
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Mucoid, Dry)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup()


gtcheck_data <- gtcheck_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pair_key = paste(sort(c(Query_Sample, Genotyped_Sample)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  ungroup() ## The idea is to put the two strains names in the same alphabeticl order no matter which one came first. So it will create an identical key of AVT29_AVT98
View(gtcheck_data)


mismatch_filtered <- merge(pairs_wide, gtcheck_data, by = "pair_key")

## I want to calculate the number of SNP differences 

mismatch_filtered <- mismatch_filtered %>%
  mutate(SNP_differences = Sites_compared - Matching_genotypes)
#View(mismatch_filtered)

mismatch_filtered

hist(mismatch_filtered$SNP_differences)



## For itols I will only extract the mismatches and pair s
mismatch_filtered
mismatch_filtered_subset <- mismatch_filtered %>% select(c("Pairs", "Mucoid", "Dry", "SNP_differences"))
mismatch_filtered_subset

SNPs_Pairs <- pivot_longer(mismatch_filtered_subset,
              cols = c(Mucoid, Dry),
             names_to = "Morphology",
             values_to = "Strains")


write_xlsx(SNPs_Pairs, here("Tables", "SNPs_Pairs.xlsx"))


```

# Genotype data: R studio section #

This will have the presence absence and the SNP data

```{r}

#### presence/absence matrix ####

# I will work with the .Rtab from the panaroo outcome. I will extract the .Rtab file from the following path: /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/Kayla/avtPacBio/panaroo_output and import them to my local computer

gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- read.delim(here("Data_input", "Genome", "gene_presence_absence.Rtab"), header = TRUE) #I opened panaroo output. In this file strains were labeled in a different way than they were labeled in the phylogenetic tree in Guha et al., 2026, so in the next steps I homogenized the labeling system 
gene_presence_absence_pyseer
gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>% select(-c("strain_NIG", "strain_EXC")) #Remove the strains that are not part of the AVT collection.

Strains <- read_excel(here("Data_input", "Strains_Description_Phenotype_Github.xlsx")) # Import the table with the AVT format labels used in Guha et al., 2026 (Strain_Code) and the the one used in this manuscript (Strain). I want the codes in these R.tab document to have the same format than Strain_Code

Strains_panaroo <- Strains %>% mutate(Strain_panaroo = paste0("strain_", Strain)) # Replicate the labeling system used in Panaroo
Strains_panaroo

## Replace the names in the gene_presence_absence_edited with the AVT1, AVT2, AVT3 names: build the rename map: names(new) = old column name, values = new column name

rename_map <- setNames(Strains_panaroo$Strain_panaroo, Strains_panaroo$Strain_Code) 
gene_presence_absence_pyseer <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>% rename(any_of(rename_map))

write_tsv(gene_presence_absence_pyseer, here("Tables", "gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer.tsv"))

## Cut the genes that are present in less than 5% and therefore also more than 95% of the strain collection

strain_cols <- names(gene_presence_absence_pyseer)[-1]
strain_cols

nrow(gene_presence_absence_pyseer) #12591 groups

gene_pa_filtered <- gene_presence_absence_pyseer %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(af = mean(c_across(all_of(strain_cols)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(af >= 0.05 & af <= 0.95) %>%
  select(-af) ## By cutting the genes that were present in more than 100% I am cutting the genes that were present in all of the strains, which is good becaues I do not want to work with genes that were invariant.

gene_pa_filtered

nrow(gene_pa_filtered) #3592

write_tsv(gene_pa_filtered, here("Tables", "gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv")) 

```

```{r}


### Turn the tree in a similarity matrix using pyseer helper script that can be obtained in pyseer github repository (https://github.com/mgalardini/pyseer). It is currently in this path: /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/pyseer. I will use the script phylogeny_distance.py  to create the kinship matrix that will be used as a random effect when I run pyseer. phylogeny_distance.py should extract the pairwise patristic distances (branch length distances between nodes) from a Newick phylogenetic tree.


python /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/pyseer/scripts/phylogeny_distance.py --lmm /storage/home/mag6678/burghardt/MariaGil/EPS_genes/panaroo/tree/AVT_single_copy_core_concat.fasta.treefile > phylogeny_similarity.tsv

### Filter the vcf file 

vcftools --vcf strain_118_variants.vcf \
  --minQ 20 --maf 0.05 --max-missing 0.8 \
  --recode --out strain_118_filtered
# This step created strain_118_filtered.log which displays information about the filtering step, and strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf, which is the vcf file after the filtering step. 

### To enable rapid regional querying, we used bgzip to sort genomic coordinates and compress them, and tabix, to generate spatial indexes. 

bgzip strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf ## Creates the document strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz

tabix -p vcf strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz ##strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz.tbi

# Script to run pyseer #

```{r, include= FALSE}

conda install bioconda::pyseer

#### Presence absence (PA)  ####

### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the binary phenotype where Mucoid is 1 and Dry is 0.

pyseer --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv \
  --distances phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv \
  --max-dimensions 8 \
  --output-patterns patterns_glm_binary_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_glm_binary_PA.txt



### Pyseer code to run the presence absence data using the continuous anthrone values where each phenotypic value is the Glucose/OD600

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --pres Data_input/gene_presence_absence_rtab_pyseer_maf05.tsv \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_Glucose_maf05_PA.txt \
  > pyseer_results_Glucose_maf05_PA.txt


#### I got a pushback regarding how have I run my analysis here, and I was suggested to run a generalized linear model. 




#### SNPs ####

In the binary phenotype in runned a generalized linear model where the population structure was accounted based on the distances stated by the 

pyseer --phenotypes Data_input/Binary_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --distances phylogeny_distance_forglm.tsv \
  --max-dimensions 8 \
  --output-patterns patterns_glm_binary_snps.txt \
  > pyseer_results_glm_binary_snps.txt


In the glucose phenotype the population structure was accounted as the kinship matrix 

pyseer --lmm --phenotypes Data_input/Glucose_phenotype_pyseer.tsv \
  --vcf Data_input/strain_118_filtered.recode.vcf.gz \
  --similarity Data_input/phylogeny_similarity.tsv \
  --output-patterns patterns_snps_glucose.txt \
  > pyseer_snp_results_glucose.txt

To calculate the number of genes/SNP variants that covary across all of the strains I used the count_patterns.py that is part of the pyseer github folder. 


Pyseer will test all the SNPs/genes, and it will simultaneously create pattern.txt files that evaluate how many distinct patterns actually exist among all the variants tested. For every tested variant, pyseer writes one line encoding that variant's presence/absence (or genotype) vector across all the strains. Two variants get written as the identical line if they have the exact same 0/1 pattern across every single strain, - same strains carrying it, same strains lacking it, no exception. 

```

Test for phylogenetic independence 

```{r}

# Testing independent origins of the dry phenotype
#
# Part 1: phylo.d (caper) -- tests whether the dry/mucoid phenotype is phylogenetically clumped (D=0, one ancestral origin retained by descent) or randomly scattered across tips (D=1, consistent with independent/convergent origins).

library(ape)
library(caper)
#install.packages("phytools")
library(phytools)
#install.packages("geiger")
library(geiger)
## Phylogenetic data

```{r}

# Root the FULL tree (117 strains + 2 outgroup strains) using the outgroups 

full_tree <- read.tree(here("Data_input", "Genome", "AVT_single_copy_core_concat_outgroup.fasta.treefile"))
full_tree #I am including the file that has three outgroups

#full_tree$tip.label

### From the .Rmd in Guha et al., 2026 I found 

full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT7827695.1"] <- "Sinorhizobium medicae USDA1037"
full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT6965.1"]    <- "Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021"
full_tree$tip.label[full_tree$tip.label == "AVT2197065.1"] <- "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"

full_tree     

tree2 <- drop.tip(full_tree, "Sinorhizobium medicae USDA1037") #I think she dropped this one because is causing problems when I try to root using the three
tree_rooted2 <- root(
  tree2,
  outgroup = c("Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021",
               "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"),
  resolve.root = TRUE
)

# 2. THEN drop the outgroups, since I have no complete phenotype data for them
analysis_tree <- drop.tip(tree_rooted2, c("Sinorhizobium meliloti RM1021", "Sinorhizobium meliloti USDA1106"))
analysis_tree


# 3. Resolve any polytomies on the now-pruned, rooted tree
analysis_tree <- multi2di(analysis_tree)
analysis_tree
analysis_tree$edge.length[analysis_tree$edge.length == 0] <- 1e-8




#tree <- read.tree(here("Data_input", "Genome", "AVT_single_copy_core_concat.fasta.treefile"))
#tree

#tree <- midpoint.root(tree) #I am going to root the tree using a midpoint
#tree <- multi2di(tree) # Resolve any remaining polytomies by randomly splitting them into a series of zero-length bifurcating branches -- this doesn't add any real evolutionary information, it just satisfies the bifurcating requirement


pheno <- Strains_pyseer
pheno

matched <- treedata(analysis_tree, setNames(pheno[["Binary_trait"]], pheno[["samples"]]),
                     sort = TRUE, warnings = TRUE)
analysis_tree <- matched$phy
analysis_tree

pheno_vec <- matched$data[, 1]  # named character vector, e.g. "Dry"/"Mucoid"
pheno_vec

cat("Tree has", Ntip(tree), "tips after matching.\n")
cat("Phenotype counts:\n")
print(table(pheno_vec))


## PART 1: phylo.d -- is the phenotype clumped or scattered on the tree?

# phylo.d needs a data.frame (not just a vector) with a binary 0/1 column, plus a comparative.data object linking that data.frame to the tree.


pheno_df <- data.frame(
  strain = names(pheno_vec),
  dry_binary = pheno_vec
)

pheno_df

is.rooted(analysis_tree)
is.binary(analysis_tree)


comp_data <- comparative.data(
  phy = tree,
  data = pheno_df,
  names.col = "strain",
  vcv = TRUE
)



d_result <- phylo.d(
  data = comp_data,
  binvar = dry_binary,
  permut = 1000
)

print(d_result)


d_summary <- data.frame(
  N_tips = length(comp_data$phy$tip.label),
  D_estimate = d_result$DEstimate,
  P_random_D1 = d_result$Pval1,
  P_brownian_D0 = d_result$Pval0,
  Permutations = 1000   # the number you set, not d_result$Permutations
                         # (that field holds the 1000 simulated null D values,
                         # not a count -- hardcode the number you specified)
)

d_summary

write.csv(d_summary, "phylo_d_supplementary_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)
